definitions.explanation: a quality of warmth or friendliness in one's manner; almost always used in the negative form 素っ気ない to mean cold, curt, or unfriendly

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{返事|へんじ}は{素|そ}っ{気|け}なかった。
{素|そ}っ{気|け}ない{態度|たいど}を{取|と}らないでほしい。
examples.english: I wish you wouldn't act so cold toward me.

examples.japanese: {店員|てんいん}に{素|そ}っ{気|け}なく{断|ことわ}られて、がっかりした。
examples.english: I was disappointed when the shop clerk curtly turned me down.

notes:
Almost exclusively used in the negative form {素|そ}っ{気|け}ない (curt, cold, unfriendly) or as the adverb {素|そ}っ{気|け}なく. The positive form {素|そ}っ{気|け} alone is rarely used. Describes a manner of speaking or behaving that lacks warmth or interest.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {素|そ}っ{気|け}ない{返事|へんじ}: a curt reply
- {素|そ}っ{気|け}ない{態度|たいど}: a cold attitude
- {素|そ}っ{気|け}なく{言|い}う: to say curtly
- {素|そ}っ{気|け}なく{断|ことわ}る: to refuse coldly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {冷|つめ}たい: cold — describes both personality and physical temperature; broader than {素|そ}っ{気|け}ない
- {愛想|あいそ}がない: unfriendly — emphasizes lack of sociability or charm
- {無愛想|ぶあいそう}: brusque, unsociable — stronger than {素|そ}っ{気|け}ない, suggesting habitual unfriendliness
